'''Divsha Amirà''' ({{Langx|he|דיבשה אמירה}}; 1899 – 9 April 1966) was an Israeli [[mathematician]] and [[Education|educator]].

==Biography==
Amirà was born in [[Brańsk]], [[Russian Empire]] to Rivka ({{nee|Garbuz}}) and Aharon Itin. She [[Aliyah|immigrated to Israel]] with her family in 1906. Her father was one of the founders of [[Tel Aviv|Ahuzat Bayit]] (today Tel Aviv), a founder of the Tel Aviv [[Great Synagogue (Tel Aviv)|Great Synagogue]], and the owner of the first [[publishing house]] in [[Jaffa]]. She graduated in the second class of the [[Herzliya Hebrew Gymnasium|Herzliya Gymnasium]] in 1914.<ref>{{cite book|editor1-first=Baruch|editor1-last=Ben-Yehuda|editor2-first=Uriel|editor2-last=Ofek|editor2-link=Uriel Ofek|title=ספורה של הגמנסיה ״הרצליה״|trans-title=The Story of the Gymnasia Herzliya|location=Tel Aviv|publisher=Gymnasia Herzliya|year=1970|language=he|oclc=745130545}}</ref>

Amirà studied at the [[University of Göttingen]] and obtained her doctorate from the [[University of Geneva]] in 1924 under the guidance of [[Herman Müntz]].<ref name=muntz>{{cite journal|title=Herman Müntz: A Mathematician's Odyssey|first1=Eduardo L.|last1=Ortiz|first2=Allan|last2=Pinkus|journal=[[Mathematical Intelligencer]]|volume=27|date=2005|pages=22&ndash;31|doi=10.1007/BF02984810|s2cid=14216180|url=https://www.math.technion.ac.il/~pinkus/papers/Muntz.pdf}}</ref> Her [[doctoral thesis]], published in 1925, provided a [[Projective geometry|projective]] synthesis of [[Euclidean geometry]].<ref>{{cite thesis|first=Divsha|last=Amirà|title=La synthèse projective de la géométrie euclidienne|location=Tel Aviv|publisher=A. Itine and S. Shoshani Press|year=1925|language=fr|oclc=247600580}}</ref>

==Pedagogic career==
After leaving Geneva, Amirà worked at [[Gymnasia Rehavia]] in [[Jerusalem]], and taught several courses on [[geometry]] at the [[Einstein Institute of Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Berlin Roots – Zionist Incarnation: The Ethos of Pure Mathematics and the Beginnings of the Einstein Institute of Mathematics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem|first=Shaul|last=Katz|journal=Science in Context|url=http://journals.cambridge.org/abstract_S0269889704000092|volume=17|issue=1–2|pages=199–234|date=2004|doi=10.1017/S0269889704000092|publisher=Cambridge University Press|s2cid=145575536|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She later taught at the {{ill|Levinsky College of Education|he|מכללת לוינסקי לחינוך}} and [[Hebrew University Secondary School|Beit-Hakerem High School]], where her students included such future mathematicians as [[Ernst G. Straus]].

==Published works==
Amirà published an introductory [[Textbook|school textbook]] on geometry in 1938, following the [[Hilbert's axioms|axiomatic approach]] of Hilbert's ''[[Grundlagen der Geometrie]]''.<ref>{{cite book|first=Divsha|last=Amirà|title=Geometry|location=Tel Aviv|publisher=‘Omanuth|year=1938|language=he|oclc=741049941}}</ref> She published a more advanced textbook on the same topic in 1963.<ref>{{cite book|first=Divsha|last=Amirà|trans-title=The Axiomatic Foundation of the Geometry Foundations|title=ביסוס אכסיומתי ליסודות הגיאומטריה|location=Tel Aviv|publisher=‘Am-‘Oved and Dvir|year=1963|language=he|oclc=233094624}}</ref>
